request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now an **Export claims (CSV)** button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) on the sheet, next to the people export. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The change is front end only, all in `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`; the server and stored data are untouched.

- **What the file holds:** the header `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then one line per claim. People come in list order, retired people included, and each person's claims run oldest first.
- **Figures match the screen:** the due and period are worked out the same way the claim rows work them out on screen. An empty number, an empty period or an `n/a` due is written as it is.
- **Quoting and line ends:** the same as the people export. A value with a comma, quote or line break is wrapped in double quotes, and every line ends with a plain line feed. I moved the people export's download code into a shared helper so both buttons use it.
- **Timing:** like the people export, the file is only made once the sheet's data has finished reloading, so it reflects what's on screen.

The file downloads as `claims-<sheet id>.csv`. Deleted claims are included because they still appear in the claim list on screen.
